name: Jed York

views.text: A coach and general manager who have taken us deep in the playoffs are not going anywhere after one bad year.
We will do everything we can to keep our quarterback for a long time.
Some offseasons are about discipline with money so the core can be paid.
Being called cheap after a roster reset does not bother me.
The goal every year is the Super Bowl.
I trust my football people to build the roster.

signatures: affirms his coach and GM at season's end
want: Finally win a sixth Super Bowl in the Shanahan-Lynch era (medium).
fear: Letting the window close through bad contracts (medium).
voice: Confident, practical and occasionally defensive about money. Speaks plainly about trust in his staff and the business side of the cap.

evidence.summary: After a losing 2024 season York said Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch were not going anywhere.
York said the team would do everything it could to keep Brock Purdy for a long time.
York framed the 2025 offseason as one of spending restraint around Purdy's pending deal and responded to being called cheap.

review.notes: Thin coverage: two to four sources found by web search (2026-11-06); sliders mostly left at 5; a few publication dates are taken from the news cycle the article covers. Draft for JR to check.
